title: Closed-Loop Neural Activation Control in Vision-Language-Action Models
models: OpenVLA on SimplerEnv BridgeData V2 tasks
action_head: discrete action tokens (OpenVLA); X-VLA uses a flow-matching head but the paper does not explain how neurons were selected for it
methods: FFN value-vector vocabulary projection and kNN concept-to-neuron matching (extends Haon et al. 2025)
per-task PPO controller over 10 neuron coefficients with reward = concept metric + lambda * task success
question: Does replacing the fixed steering coefficient of FFN-neuron steering with a feedback controller (PID or RL) keep task success while still steering height and speed?
key_findings: Static steering at C=20 collapses success: average LIBERO SR drops from 71.37% (unsteered) to 27.37% for height and 1.8% for speed steering.
PID keeps average SR near baseline (71% height, 72.5% speed); RL controller reaches 73.88% (height) and 76.12% (speed), above the unsteered policy.

But on LIBERO the steering effect itself is near zero or reversed: LIBERO-Long mean height 0.832 m unsteered vs 0.828 (PID) and 0.804 (RL); AAT 181.7 vs 184.5 vs 181.9; mean speed 11.26 cm/s unsteered vs 10.88 (PID) and 11.04 (RL); SAT 2.69 vs 2.60 vs 2.54 (Tables 3-4). Other suites show differences of similar size within large SDs.
Static C=20 'up' steering lowers LIBERO-Long mean height (0.832 -> 0.723 m) instead of raising it.
On SimplerEnv/BridgeData V2 the effect is visible: height AAT 39.15 -> 47.28 (PID) / 48.13 (RL), speed 16.93 -> 18.90 / 21.38 cm/s, SR 40% -> 46-49% (Table 2).
X-VLA on LIBERO-Goal: AAT 161.58 -> 183.35 (PID) / 400.33 (RL) with SR 59% -> 60%; static C=20 gives AAT 626.74 but SR 25% (Table 1).
RL without PID warm start: SR 75% -> 65% and SAT 2.48 -> 2.28 (main text); per-suite SR drop e.g. LIBERO-Long 66.5 -> 57.0 (App. Table 5).

evidence.scale: 20 deterministic seeded rollouts per task (App. D); 10 tasks per LIBERO suite; one fine-tuned OpenVLA per suite; RL controller trained per task
evidence.statistics: no tests; mean +/- SD of steering metrics only; no CIs on success rates
evidence.baselines: unsteered OpenVLA; static steering of Haon et al. with C = 5, 10, 20 (per-task best alpha chosen in task-wise tables)

causal_validation: Interventions are causal by construction (scaling FFN neuron activations), but the paper does not test whether the selected 'motion' neurons are specific: no random-neuron control, no ablation. The tables show that on LIBERO the closed-loop controllers barely move the targeted metric.
closed_loop: Yes, all metrics come from closed-loop simulated rollouts; the controller itself also uses online state feedback.
limitations_stated: RL controller is trained per task.
Neuron identification still involves manual filtering.
Only a small set of steering concepts (height, speed).
critique: The central claim, 'better steering-task success trade-off', is not supported on LIBERO: the closed-loop variants keep success mainly by hardly steering, and their height and speed are at or below the unsteered model in the paper's own tables.
The RL controller is optimized per task with a task-success reward, so success above baseline may be ordinary RL fine-tuning through a 10-dim action space, not evidence about the concept neurons.

Static 'up' steering lowering height suggests the vocabulary-selected neurons do not encode height in this model, which undercuts the interpretability premise; no random-neuron baseline to check specificity.
Simulation only, OpenVLA only in depth; the X-VLA transfer is one table without explanation of how vocabulary projection applies to a flow-matching model.
No statistical tests with 20 rollouts per task; LIBERO-Object heights (~0.21 m vs ~1.06 m elsewhere) suggest inconsistent coordinate frames across suites.
one_line: Wraps vocabulary-selected OpenVLA FFN neurons in a PID or per-task RL controller so steering does not wreck task success, but on LIBERO the controlled runs barely change height or speed.
